# ASTRA X HIGH — Rational-point rigidity and effective affine smoothing

**Date:** 2026-10-09 (AEST)  
**Status:** Explicit unconditional reduction, with primary-literature comparisons; no historically verified novel or 10/10 result. The undecidability corollary is conditional on the validity of the OpenAI H10(Q) proof.

**Proposition (proof reconstructed here; historical novelty UNVERIFIED).** Given a nonconstant polynomial `f ∈ Q[X_1,...,X_n]` of degree `d ≥ 1`, an algorithm returns a positive integer `m` and an affine hypersurface

    H_{f,m}:  Z - Z^3 = m^2 f(X_1,...,X_n)^2

such that:

1. `H_{f,m}` is smooth over `Q` (hence geometrically smooth).
2. `H_{f,m}` is geometrically integral (absolutely irreducible).
3. `H_{f,m}(Q) = V(f)(Q) × {-1,0,1}` as rational point sets.
4. Its total degree is `max(3,2d)` and it uses only one more variable than `f`.
5. Consequently `#H_{f,m}(Q) = 3 #V(f)(Q)` whenever the cardinality is finite, with the evident statement for infinite sets.

Constant inputs can be preprocessed: replace `f=0` by the nonconstant polynomial `X`, and replace a nonzero constant by `X^2+1` (with a new variable). These have matching rational solvability.

# SOL/A — Finite-power Bernoullicity investigation

## 1. Status of the primary problem

No exact Bernoulli conjugacy has been established. In particular, I have not proved that \\(K^m\\) is Bernoulli for any finite \\(m\\), nor obtained \\(2^G\cong_G4^G\\).

The central difficulty is stronger than constructing arbitrarily many independent Bernoulli factors. It is to construct an independent generating process whose translates recover all of \\(K^m\\), modulo null sets.

A relevant general problem was explicitly formulated by Tim Austin in The Geometry of Model Spaces for Probability-Preserving Actions of Sofic Groups (2016):

> Is every complemented factor of a Bernoulli system itself Bernoulli?

Austin identified this as unresolved for nonamenable groups at the time. 

[image](https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=https://www.researchgate.net\&sz=32)

ResearchGate



Your action has additional structure: \\(K\\) is a finite-range algebraic factor, and the inherited identity

\\[ X\cong_G X\times K \\]

makes it an independently complemented factor of a Bernoulli shift. Thus a theorem establishing Bernoullicity for these particular algebraic retracts would solve a substantially more structured problem than arbitrary Bernoulli-factor classification.

The existence of non-Bernoulli factors of Bernoulli shifts, demonstrated through Popa's constructions, does not settle this case: those examples do not automatically possess the required independent complement. 

[image](https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=https://www.researchgate.net\&sz=32)

ResearchGate

There is a rigorous structural theorem that does not require the inherited coloring lemma.

Theorem (free-subgroup Bernoulli restriction). Suppose

\\[ ab=1,\qquad p=1-ba\ne0 \\]

in \\(\mathbb F_2[G]\\), and let \\(K=\ker T_a\\). If \\(H\leq G\\) is a free subgroup of infinite index, then

\\[ \boxed{ K\\!\restriction_H\ \cong_H\ (\mathbb F_2^{\mathbb N})^H } \\]

# Intake clarification; separate from immutable authored reports

No independent proof reconstruction, scientific diagnostic replay, external correctness or priority certification occurred in this intake.

SOL/A free-subgroup proof: the final rank inference needs the finite-coset-support argument, not the unrestricted assertion that a free module containing infinitely many independent vectors must have infinite rank over a noncommutative ring. If Rp were finitely generated over k[H], finitely many generators would occupy finitely many left-H-coset coordinates in R; all their k[H]-linear combinations stay in that same finite coordinate union. The constructed g_i p have pairwise disjoint nonempty coordinate supports, contradicting finite generation. With the imported FIR submodule-freeness theorem and countability, this yields countably infinite free rank. This is an elementary intake clarification of a written inference, not a source audit receipt or validation of the whole theorem. Independently check the exact FIR theorem and convolution/duality conventions.

Retain the infinite-index free-subgroup hypothesis explicitly. The report's cyclic consequence additionally requires infinite index; torsion-freeness alone is not that hypothesis. A separate argument using the actual witness would be needed to discharge it.

The random equivariant basis criterion is sufficient and conditionally linear; it is not equivalent to all measurable Bernoulli conjugacies. Independence and spanning are both mandatory. No random basis or effective construction is provided. The inherited finite-defect splitting lemma is explicitly audit-deferred by SOL/A, so its report does not independently validate N252.

Affine smoothing is a source-reconstructed unconditional reduction; the degree-at-most-eight undecidability corollary is conditional on the unverified pinned H10(Q) theorem.
